newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African money mkt shortage jumps to 5-month high. [CORRECTED 10:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S.African money mkt shortage jumps to 5-month high. [CORRECTED 10:45 GMT]

text.p: South Africa's money market shortage rose to its highest level in five months on Wednesday, taking dealers by surprise as it climbed over one billion rand to just below 10 billion.
Dealers said the squeeze was mostly likely due to a mismatch of flows, heightened by a steady stream of notes flowing out of the system during the school holiday period.

Figures released on Thursday show the money market shortage climbing to 9.936 billion rand on Wednesday -- its highest levels since April 30 when it touched an all-time high of 10.955 billion, according to the Reserve Bank.
"There was a little bit of a misjudgement on the government spending which they thought would be a bit more," a money market dealer said.
"And they did not put enough money in the tax and loan account to counter this."
Another dealer said: "We were taken by surprise. I think even the SARB (South African Reserve Bank) was taken by surprise."
But traders said the shortage was likely to return to more realistic levels by the beginning of next week, obviating the need to raise short-term money market rates.

"The whole thing is technical, it is not a new trend...The word we are getting from the central bank is that the shortage will come down quite a bit from next week...back to the 7.5 to eight billion rand level."
Standard Bank raised its three-month NCD rate on the offer side by five basis points to 15.80, while Nedcor lifted its rate by the same margin to 15.75 percent on the offer side.
The 90-day BA rate was quoted in a 15.35 to 15.20 percent range from 15.30 to 15.15 percent on Wednesday.
(Corrects to clarify rate rise and adds details of other bank rate movements.)
Dealers said foreign purchases of South African rands and gilts this week would help the shortage move down from its heady levels.

"We can also see the way the rand is strengthening, there is some cash coming in from foreigners. They have been buying gilts and equities so there will be some cash inflows next week," a dealer said.
